title: Tucker matrix-bank Mirror layer coefficients
hypothesis: When layer coefficients over a shared Tucker matrix bank follow a compact Givens orbit, replacing free per-layer coefficients with a shared vector and angle addresses reduces total model payload while preserving layer functions; generic rank-2 PCA is the mandatory control.
physical_object: shared bank of K=8 matrices of shape 32x32 used across L=64 logical layers
mirror_coordinate: one shared 8-vector and one Givens angle per layer
controls: Tucker shared bank plus free layer coefficients
shared Mirror vector and per-layer angle

development.selection_metric: matrix and functional NRMSE, actual total serialized bytes, code fitting wall time

paid_objects: full matrices fp16 or coefficient codes/factors fp16

success_gate: Aligned functional NRMSE <=0.01 with >=10% lower total bytes than free Tucker coefficients; generic PCA matching Mirror means no Mirror-specific value. Independent coefficients measure the boundary.
failure_gate: Mirror misses aligned quality/byte gate or does not improve the fixed-byte frontier; independent tasks requiring private coefficients are a boundary result.
boundaries: Teacher aligned stratum is generated from Givens orbit
No pretrained Transformer or natural layer weights
All methods evaluated after fp16 serialization and deterministic decode
